definitions.explanation: Both of two companies already mentioned, as in a merger, a partnership, or a dispute. Common in business news.

examples.japanese: {両社|りょうしゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦{合併|がっぺい}→合併：04778_gappei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The two companies will merge next year.

examples.japanese: {両社|りょうしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{記者会見|きしゃかいけん}→記者会見：19954_kishakaiken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}いた→開く：01979_hiraku⟧。
examples.english: The presidents of both companies held a press conference.

examples.japanese: ⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{長引|ながび}いた→長引く：14473_nagabiku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{最終的|さいしゅうてき}→最終的：13013_saishuuteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{両社|りょうしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{合意|ごうい}→合意：05093_goui⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The negotiations dragged on, but in the end both companies agreed.

notes:
⟦{両|りょう}→両：11182_ryou⟧〜 means 'both' and attaches to a short noun: {両社|りょうしゃ}, ⟦{両国|りょうこく}→両国：10010_ryoukoku⟧ (both countries), ⟦{両者|りょうしゃ}→両者：11357_ryousha⟧ (both parties).

WATCH OUT:
⟦{両者|りょうしゃ}→両者：11357_ryousha⟧ (both parties, both people) has the same reading. In speech, context tells them apart; {両社|りょうしゃ} is used only for companies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {両社|りょうしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{合併|がっぺい}→合併：04778_gappei⟧: the merger of the two companies
- {両社|りょうしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{提携|ていけい}→提携：05773_teikei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: the two companies form a partnership
- {両社|りょうしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧: relations between the two companies
